clue.text: Crowd into a thousand and one evening entertainments

indicators.note: the crowd word is pushed into the middle of the other letters, so into marks a container

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
to crowd is to press

explanation.surface: A huge crowd squeezes into a thousand and one nights of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS goes inside A + K + I, giving A-PRESS-KI.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising and partying that follows a day on the slopes, typically in the evening.

clue.text: Preferable for a bigwig

definitions.meaning: as in you might just ..., meaning it would be better

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying one may as well do something makes it the better option, and a swell is a toff or important figure.

clue.text: Put about — later I put about

indicators.note: put about the second time means the letters are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Spread the rumour, then I spread it again later.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail gossip is to pass it on or spread it.

clue.text: The leaders of some parties properly animated

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the next two words

parts.note: rightly means properly or correctly

explanation.surface: Some party leaders are suitably lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy.

clue.text: Understand the procedure when poker's to get organised

indicators.note: get organised means the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Knowing the routine for when a card game needs setting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get organised' rearranges WHEN POKERS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing the ropes is an idiom for being familiar with how things are done.

clue.text: Jack's brother about to imbibe

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, an AB (able seaman), so jack's gives AB plus the S

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the brother word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor's brother is about to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a sailor, an able seaman (AB). 'about' turns the brother word backwards; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or take in, the same as imbibing.

clue.text: Money raised by word of mouth .

indicators.note: word of mouth means the word is spoken, so we want one that sounds the same

parts.note: children raised are bred

explanation.surface: Funds collected through people telling each other.
explanation.walkthrough: BREAD is slang for money. The dots join this clue to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is old slang for cash.

clue.text: … Spoken about one type of card game and a card

indicators.note: about means the spoken word goes round the other letters

parts.note: oral means spoken
I is the Roman numeral one
gin rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: Spoken words about a card game and a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a playing card, but it is an eccentric person. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an eccentric or amusing person, and so is an original.

clue.text: Confuse the heart 'of Robert Thornton

indicators.note: the heart is the central pair of letters in the name Robert

parts.note: Thornton Wilder was the American playwright of Our Town

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what lies at the heart of a man called Robert Thornton.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to baffle or perplex them.

clue.text: Battle station

definitions.meaning: the 1815 battle at which Wellington defeated Napoleon

explanation.walkthrough: WATERLOO station is one of London's main rail terminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo names both Napoleon's final defeat in Belgium and the London rail terminus named after it.

clue.text: Clergyman — one we turned to have another look at

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: turned means the word we is flipped to read backwards

explanation.surface: A vicar, along with one of our number, turned back to take a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EW from WE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To review something is to examine it again.

clue.text: Homer may well get mistaken for a smaller bird

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet, or a cartoon father, might confuse one bird for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get mistaken' rearranges HOMER MAY WELL; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowhammer is a small bunting with a bright yellow head.

clue.text: Situated in Italy, in Genoa

indicators.note: the first in says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Somewhere located in Italy, specifically in Genoa.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across itaLY IN Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying describes where something is placed or located, as a town lying on a river.

clue.text: All term I'd worked on this — I got nowhere

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters have been worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A student laments a whole term of effort that achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges ALL TERM I'D. The definition is the description of a machine on which you walk or run without moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym treadmill keeps you walking while you stay in the same spot, the image of effort with no progress.

clue.text: High School in London accepts characters from, each race

parts.note: a steep price is a high one

indicators.note: accepts means the school's letters take in other letters

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics

indicators.note: the characters taken from the word each are used in a shuffled order

explanation.surface: A top London school welcomes pupils from every race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters from' asks for the letters of 'each' in a new order, and 'accepts' puts them inside the London school's initials. The LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences, or an athletics event over hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: Rosie, say, in motor race

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race or people can be a nation

explanation.surface: A girl named Rosie takes part in a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'Rosie' reads as a girl's name but means something rosy-pink, like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnation is a rosy pink flesh colour, so it is an example of something rosy.

clue.text: Sinks where the water runs away

definitions.meaning: to sink a ship or a plan, to ruin it
holes in a ship's side that drain water off the deck

explanation.definitionFit: To scupper is to wreck or sink, and scuppers are the drainage holes along a ship's deck.

clue.text: Emancipated worker's carte blanche

parts.note: emancipated means set free
a hand is a worker, as a farm hand

explanation.surface: A freed labourer is given full authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche is complete freedom to act as one wishes.

clue.text: Girl we hear presuming to transfer figures

indicators.note: we hear tells us the girl's name is only spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
forward means presumptuous, so presuming gives it

explanation.surface: A pushy girl tries to move numbers around the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. In accounting, totals are moved from one page or period to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, a balance is carried forward when it is moved onto the next page or period.

clue.text: American city displaying airy sculpture

definitions.meaning: a hanging artwork of balanced parts that move in the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is a city in Alabama, and a mobile is a suspended kinetic sculpture like Calder's.

clue.text: Standard stopper?

definitions.meaning: one who bans or forbids things, read whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag, and whimsically someone who bans things puts a stop to them.

clue.text: Strange things brought about by flower power

indicators.note: brought about suggests turning things round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an anemone is a flower
HP, horsepower, is a measure of power

explanation.surface: Odd events caused by the hippie flower power movement.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: 'brought about' rearranges ANEMONE plus HP, letters not printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels.

clue.text: Summer visitor's vehicle coming off the roundabout

indicators.note: coming off means the vehicle is taken away from the roundabout word

parts.note: a carousel is a fairground roundabout
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's car leaving a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' is a link. A fairground roundabout, not a road junction. The ring ousel visits Britain in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring ousel, a thrush, is a migrant bird that breeds in Britain in summer.

clue.text: Bouquet featuring, amongst roses, other more advanced heads

indicators.note: heads are the front letters of the listed words

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers with superior blooms in among the roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouquet is the scent of wine, a synonym for aroma.

clue.text: Go and change, please

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in please

explanation.surface: Someone is asked politely to leave and get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to go by or pass, which is what it does when it elapses.

clue.text: Confines to one bowling end

parts.note: the ambit of something is its bounds or limits
I is the Roman numeral one
a bowler who is bowling is said to be on

explanation.surface: A cricketer is kept to bowling from just one end of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. In cricket a bowler currently in action is 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: An end in the sense of a goal or aim is one's ambition.

clue.text: Lumber, borne by a horse

definitions.meaning: to lumber someone is to burden them with something
the seat a horse carries for its rider

explanation.definitionFit: To saddle someone with a task is to burden them, and the rider's seat is strapped on a horse's back.

clue.text: State in which relation regretted having returned

parts.note: a gran is a relation, a grandmother

indicators.note: returned means the regretted word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: A relative went back to a place she regretted leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having returned' reverses RUED to DEUR; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: State in the sense of pomp and ceremony, as lying in state, means splendour.
